scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together. I'm a Christian, so I want to make sure my decisions align with my faith. Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. My girlfriend and I have been dating for three years, and we've had a good relationship except for this issue. She's a student working part-time, barely making enough to cover her rent and school fees. I'm 24, working a minimum wage plus commission job, and I don't have much savings. She doesn't ask me for money, which I appreciate, but she's worried that I'm too focused on helping my family instead of building a future together. My family is really close, and I feel a strong responsibility to take care of them. Recently, my mom received a settlement of about $100k, bought a house and a new car. Despite this, I still feel the need to help them, which she doesn't understand. She thinks I should focus on my own future, especially since I'm trying to get my real estate license but can't find the time because my family is so demanding. They get angry or sad when I'm not around for family events, and I understand why because we're a close family. I told her all this, and she got angry, saying she's not asking me to abandon my family but just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before worrying about helping my family. She feels like I can't build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving for a down payment on a house while she finishes her degree and can start helping too. But I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a really heated fight, the worst we've ever had. She said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and that I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her. She can't be with someone who doesn't prioritize that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future, that's my choice, but she's going to have to worry about herself and plan a future where she's her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Now she's stopped mentioning anything about it and is talking about saving up for a one-bedroom apartment and a car for herself. She seems so sad, but I can't help but feel like she's wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I don't know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together. From a Christian perspective, I know that family is important, but so is my relationship with my spouse. The Bible talks about honoring parents and loving your neighbor, but it also emphasizes the importance of marriage and the covenant between a husband and wife. I'm wondering if I'm putting my family above my commitment to her, which might not be healthy for our relationship. I also need to consider the practical aspects. If I'm always focusing on my family, am I neglecting our future together? She's trying to build her life, finish her degree, and wants to start a family. If I'm not contributing financially or emotionally to that, it could create a lot of tension and resentment. On the other hand, my family has been there for me, and I feel a duty to support them. But I also need to evaluate whether my involvement is healthy for both my family and our relationship. Maybe there's a middle ground where I can support my family without neglecting my responsibilities to her. I should also think about communication. Have I explained to her why my family is so important to me? Have I listened to her concerns and tried to understand her perspective? It seems like we had a fight, but maybe we need to have a more constructive conversation about how we can both support each other's goals and commitments. Another thing to consider is the future. If we decide to get married, how will our roles and responsibilities be balanced? It's important to have a shared vision for the future, and if I'm not on the same page as her, that could cause problems down the line. I also wonder about the role of sacrifice in a relationship. Both partners need to be willing to make sacrifices for each other. If I'm only focusing on my family, am I making enough sacrifices for her and our future together? Or is she expecting me to prioritize her without considering my other commitments? I should also reflect on whether my actions are causing her emotional pain. She seems sad and is planning a future without me, which is a serious issue. If I continue to prioritize my family over her, it might lead to the breakdown of our relationship, which I don't want. Maybe I need to set boundaries with my family. They get angry or sad when I'm not around, but I also have responsibilities to my girlfriend. It's possible that my family doesn't understand the importance of my relationship, and I might need to communicate that to them as well. In terms of practical steps, perhaps I can find a way to help my family without neglecting my responsibilities to her. Maybe I can set aside specific times for family and other times for her and our future. Or maybe I can find a way to contribute financially without it taking up too much of my time or energy. I also need to assess my own priorities. Is helping my family more important than building a future with her? Or can I find a balance where both are important? It's a tough question, and I need to be honest with myself about what I value most. From a Christian standpoint, I should also consider the teachings about love and commitment. The Bible says to love your neighbor as yourself, but it also emphasizes the importance of marital commitment. I need to make sure that I'm not neglecting my duties to my wife (if we were married) or my girlfriend in this case. I think the key here is balance. It's possible to care for family and build a future with a partner, but it requires careful planning, communication, and prioritization. I need to work with her to find a way that both our needs are met, even if it means making some compromises. In conclusion, while it's important to support my family, I also need to consider the impact on my relationship with my girlfriend. I shouldn't neglect her needs and our future together. It's possible that I'm being too focused on my family and not giving enough attention to building our life together, which could be causing her pain. I need to have an open and honest conversation with her to understand her perspective and find a way to balance both aspects of my life.
